problem: It says the tree is 'shown in the figure after Section 1', but the figure actually sits after Section 3, between the exam traps and the worked example. A student turning pages to find it will be confused.
fix: Say 'shown in the figure above (after Section 3)' or simply 'shown in the figure'.

problem: Edge labels are attached to the child to name the production used at the parent: the depth-1 E carries 'E → E + T', which is the root's production. But the depth-1 T (also a child of the root) carries 'T → T × F', which is not the root's production; the root's production is E → E + T. The labeling convention is inconsistent within one figure.
fix: Label the depth-1 T child with 'E → E + T' (the root's production), and keep 'T → T × F' only on the child T of the inner T node.

problem: 'The number of derivations of a string grows with the number of variables' is vague: it is the number of variables still present in the sentential form at a given step (i.e. how many independent expansions are pending) that multiplies the orders, not the number of variables in the grammar.
fix: Write: 'At any step, if the sentential form holds several variables, any of them may be expanded next, so the number of derivation orders grows with the number of variables waiting in the sentential form.'

problem: 'leftmost derivation parser' is not a standard name; a reader who searches for it will find nothing useful.
fix: Replace with 'LL parser' (the parser that follows a leftmost derivation), keeping 'abstract syntax tree' and 'Earley parser'.
